The hidden cost of bench soldering

Your soldering bench is a quality and labor problem in disguise

The bench looks cheap — a few irons and operators. But every hand-soldered joint carries a defect risk and a labor cost that compound with volume.

Output follows headcount

Each operator adds a few hundred joints per hour. Growing output means hiring more hands, not improving the process.

Quality drifts with fatigue

By the second half of the shift, tip angles and dwell times drift. Defects cluster exactly where supervision is thinnest.

Cold joints cost twice

A cold joint fails at test, needs hand rework, and the rework itself risks the board. It is the most expensive joint to make.

Solder wire disappears

Hand feeding over-uses wire, and uncontrolled tip temperature burns tips early — consumable costs nobody tracks.

Skill is a turnover risk

A skilled solderer is months of training. Every resignation resets the quality curve of your bench.

The bench sets the pace

If hand soldering is your bottleneck, no amount of SMT speed upstream changes the output at the end.

Equipment options

Four base configurations, one robot family

The S-C5331R family is available in the configurations below; stroke, drive and accessories are matched to your soldering points.

Entry configuration

Compact single-head, single-station layout with a 200×200×200×100 mm working stroke — suited to small workpieces and light duty.

Maximum throughput

Two heads and two stations with a 500×300×300×200 mm (X×Y×Z×R) stroke, up to 500 mm/s positioning speed and ±0.02 mm repeat — the recommended high-volume configuration.

Safety & fume containment

Enclosed machine with protective cover for operator safety and fume containment in stricter factory environments.

Two processes on one frame

Dual systems on one frame allow different soldering processes at front and back for complex boards.

Stepper or servo

Stepper motors for cost-effective standard joints; servo drive for fine-pitch and high-precision work.

Tips, fixtures, solder breaker

Custom soldering tips and PCB fixtures designed from your samples; solder breaker and cleaning box for consistent wire feed and tip condition.

Installation guide

From bench to production in five steps

Installation and training are included free with every S-C5331R.

01 · Bench & fixture

Place the robot on a stable workbench. We design the PCB fixture to your boards — panel size, support points and clearance for the tip.

02 · Utilities

Connect 220 V mains power (full-voltage AC110–220 V on the S-HX331R). No compressed air is required for standard operation; prepare soldering wire and tips.

03 · Programming

Set soldering temperature (0–500 °C), teach paths with the handheld teaching box, and store programs — capacity for more than 100 sets.

04 · Trial run

Solder sample boards, then tune temperature, feed speed and tip height until every joint passes your acceptance criteria.

05 · Training & ramp

Free installation and operator training included; 24/7 worldwide support and 1-day spare-part lead time after handover.

Technical evaluation FAQ

Questions buyers ask before ordering

How does the dual-table system work?

Two work tables (Y1/Y2) run in one cycle. The operator loads fixtures on one table while the robot solders the other, then the tables swap — verified at 18 pads on both tables in a 27-second cycle. Output per station roughly doubles versus a single-table robot.

What soldering methods does it support?

Spot soldering and drag soldering, with program-controlled tin feeding. A rotatable option adds an R axis for angled and side-entry joints, and a cleaning box keeps the tip in condition during long runs.

What temperature range and accuracy?

0–500 °C with a precise temperature controller. The tip recovers to set temperature in about 0.1 s, so heat-sucking pads do not cause cold joints.

How is it programmed?

With the HD handheld teaching box: set temperature, teach the soldering path, store the program. Operators learn the machine in about one day, and new boards are taught in minutes.

What utilities does it need?

220 V mains power and a stable workbench rated for the 68 kg machine. No compressed air is required for standard operation. You provide the soldering wire, tips and PCB fixtures — Southern Machinery can design the fixtures from your samples.

How do I get a price, delivery and ROI estimate?

Email info@smthelp.com or WhatsApp +86 136 0256 2576 with your board samples or drawings, joint count per board and monthly volume. Configuration, quotation and ROI estimate are provided after technical confirmation — typically within 24 hours.
